lane.name: Grunge and '90s alt radio
lane.definition: Nirvana, Pearl Jam, Soundgarden, Mudhoney, Screaming Trees: the Seattle line and its radio aftermath.

albums.label: Sub Pop
albums.description: A six-song fuzz-pedal manifesto that helped define grunge's sound, all Stooges-worship distortion and slacker sneer. Mark Arm's yowl over Steve Turner's wall of fuzz made this one of Sub Pop's defining early statements, for anyone who likes their rock sludgy and sarcastic.
albums.lineage: The true ground-zero record of the Seattle line (X8), growing directly from the noise-rock/underground scene of V16 without ever crossing into the Core's twang.

albums.label: Sub Pop
albums.description: Nirvana's murky, sludgy Sub Pop debut, all detuned riffs and Melvins-indebted heaviness before Cobain's pop instincts fully emerged. The rawest document of the pre-fame Seattle scene.
albums.lineage: Grows out of the noise-rock and underground scene near V16 and the SST/college-radio DIY network, opening the Seattle grunge line (X8) that would explode into mainstream alt-radio rather than feed the Core.

albums.label: DGC Records
albums.description: The record that took grunge mainstream, fusing pop hooks with distorted dynamics on a Butch Vig production that polished the Pixies' quiet-loud formula into a cultural phenomenon. The single most consequential alt-rock album of the era.
albums.lineage: The commercial explosion point of the Seattle line (X8), turning underground-rock roots shared with V16 into '90s mainstream alt-radio, a path that runs parallel to rather than through the Core.

albums.label: Epic
albums.description: Eddie Vedder's classic-rock-indebted baritone over widescreen, arena-scaled grunge, closer to heartland rock's earnestness than Nirvana's punk lineage. Its blend of confessional lyrics and guitar-solo bombast made it grunge's other multi-platinum debut.
albums.lineage: A Seattle-scene record within X8 that leans on the same classic-rock instincts as V20's Crazy Horse universe, feeding '90s alt radio rather than the Core.

albums.label: A&M
albums.description: A heavier, Sabbath-and-Zeppelin-indebted entry in the grunge canon, built on odd time signatures and Chris Cornell's operatic wail. Helped usher grunge into hard-rock radio alongside Nirvana and Pearl Jam.
albums.lineage: A metal-leaning branch of the Seattle scene within X8, drawing on the same noise-rock underground as V16 but pushing toward hard rock rather than the Core.

albums.label: Epic
albums.description: A more classic-rock-tinged entry from the eastern-Washington band, pairing Mark Lanegan's deep baritone with psychedelic, Crazy Horse-adjacent guitar work. Its blend of grunge heaviness and '60s/'70s rock songcraft makes it the most song-first record of the Seattle wave.
albums.lineage: A Crazy Horse-tinged outlier within X8's Seattle scene, closer in guitar tone to V20 than to punk-rooted grunge, though its commercial path still runs through '90s alt radio rather than the Core.

albums.label: DGC Records
albums.description: A deliberately abrasive, Steve Albini-recorded reaction to Nevermind's polish, full of harsh dynamics and unresolved dissonance. Widely considered Nirvana's artistic peak and a bridge back toward the noisier underground it came from.
albums.lineage: Loops the Seattle line back toward the noise-rock aesthetic of V16 via Albini's production, without leaving the X8 lane's mainstream alt-radio orbit.

albums.label: Epic
albums.description: A rawer, more urgent follow-up to Ten, trading some of the debut's polish for tighter, angrier songs. Dave Abbruzzese's harder-hitting drums and more percussive, funk-edged riffs push Vedder into a snarl, making it the band's most aggressive early record.
albums.lineage: Continues Pearl Jam's classic-rock-leaning wing of X8's Seattle scene, staying in '90s alt radio rather than crossing toward the Core.

albums.label: A&M
albums.description: Soundgarden's chart-topping peak, expanding their sludgy riffing into more melodic, psychedelic songwriting on hits like 'Black Hole Sun.' The commercial apex of grunge's early-'90s takeover of rock radio.
albums.lineage: The mainstream apex of X8's metal-leaning Seattle branch, fully embedded in '90s alt radio rather than the Core.
